meta_title: Choco Alternative for Food Distributors in 2026
meta_desc: Keep Choco and add voice ordering beside it. Your accounts speak each order into an app and approve every line. A Choco alternative that replaces nothing.
text: Saved on each order that moves off the phone
Is how long setup runs for most
Covers the hours your desk does not
Why teams look for an alternative to Choco

Choco calls itself an AI platform for food and beverage wholesalers. It turns incoming orders into digital ones, runs an online catalog that recommends products, and includes sales tools and a customer database (CRM) for foodservice. None of that is a flaw. A Choco alternative search usually starts with one small gap. Replacing a whole platform to fix it is far too much.
Some kitchens never take to tapping through an app

Every ordering platform has some accounts that keep calling, texting or leaving a voicemail at 10pm. They like the person on the other end more than a screen of buttons, and those are the orders that still eat your morning.
AI reads the message, but the kitchen never checks what it read

Choco's OrderAgent lifts an order out of a voicemail, a text, even a snapshot of a handwritten pad, which is a genuinely clever bit of engineering. But the cook who left that note never saw the lines your desk ended up with.
You want a single fix, not all new software
Swapping Choco out would mean rebuilding the storefront, the sales routine and the customer records your reps lean on. That is a lot of change to buy when the trouble is the telephone.
The Choco alternative that leaves Choco in place
Orders built by whoever is in the cooler

Your account opens the app, presses to speak, and says what the kitchen is short of. Every item appears as a line with a quantity against it. They review it, change what needs changing, and only then does it leave.
Nothing is sent until your customer has looked at the list
Works from the cooler or the prep bench, at any hour
Saves 20 to 30 minutes compared with the same order by phone
Reps stop writing up reorders from accounts on the app, so that time goes into selling
One item list per account, built from yours
Pass us the guides you keep per customer. We load them with your SKUs and the price you set for that account, so each spoken item is matched to your own SKU.
A kitchen only ever sees what it actually buys
The catalog and the pricing stay yours to set
Edit a list once and it holds on the orders after
No browsing and no shopping cart
It arrives however your office likes it
Your office does not change how it works. A finished order goes out as an email with a PDF, Excel or Word file attached, or straight into your ERP over the API, over EDI, or into QuickBooks.
Addressed to a rep, or to the purchasing desk
Over EDI, the API or QuickBooks, nobody on your team retypes it
Picking, billing and delivery carry on unchanged
You do not have to remove any software first
Stock you can see while the orders arrive

VoiceOrder Solutions shows real-time inventory visibility tied to what is being ordered, and the catalog updates as stock levels change. It does not replace your stock system: that stays in charge, and a demo shows how the levels connect.
Every line you carry, not only the quick movers
Fewer stockout surprises on a late, heavy order
Stock numbers come from the system you count with today
We never count or buy stock for you
How Choco and VoiceOrder Solutions split the work
We are not a Choco replacement, and we would rather you did not treat us as one. Our app adds on, so your storefront stays exactly as it is while you try it.
Let the catalog sell, and let voice take the order
A storefront that suggests items works best for a kitchen buyer who has time to browse. A quick reorder at the end of a shift is a different moment. The two can work together.
Give each account the way in it prefers
Kitchens that are happy tapping through Choco's app can stay there. Offer the voice app to the ones who still call or text, which is where speaking the order helps most.
Orders land where they already land
Whatever you add, the order still arrives into the system you chose, or as an email to your desk. Nobody has to learn a new screen to receive it.
See where voice ordering fits beside Choco
Twenty minutes. One spoken order, beginning to end, and how much time it can save on each order.
Short enough to finish this week
There is no data project to start, and nothing inside Choco changes. You send item lists, we set the customers up, and your customers begin sending orders.
A spreadsheet is fine. Each account's items and your prices go into a single admin screen, lined up with your SKUs.
We set up each account, and the customer downloads the app. Most have sent something in by the end of the day.
The customer has approved it, and it carries a number and the time it was sent, in the format your system takes.

Adding voice ordering should not take anything away, and the table below is drawn to show it. Most searches for a Choco alternative start with one gap, not a broken platform, so below is Choco today, then Choco with our app beside it. The two do not connect, and everything said about Choco comes from their own site.
Kitchens order by speaking into an app
Tap to order in their app
The person ordering checks each line before it sends
Voicemails, texts and photos of notes turned into orders
Each account has its own list, at your prices
Order number and time stamped on arrival
Orders come in after your office closes
Orders reach the system you already run
Better than Choco, or best used with it?
Do I need a Choco alternative to get voice ordering?

No. You can keep Choco exactly as it is and add VoiceOrder Solutions next to it. Accounts keen to talk get our app; the ones happy in Choco's app stay put. Nothing has to be switched off first, and nothing in Choco has to change.
Would that make VoiceOrder Solutions a Choco competitor?

Only in the narrow sense that both take orders. We do not run storefronts, sales tools or a CRM, and we do not want you to give those up. Most people who search for a Choco alternative want one thing added: an order the kitchen speaks and approves. They do not want a platform taken away.
Is VoiceOrder Solutions better than Choco?

No, not at what Choco is built for: larger orders, tools for reps and customer records. We are stronger at one narrower job. The customer approves every item before it goes, so nobody at your end interprets a message. That is why we belong beside Choco, not in its place.
Does VoiceOrder Solutions connect to Choco?
No. The two are separate products, and each vendor supports only its own. Each one sends its own orders into your system. Ours come in the formats shown above, which your desk knows how to handle.
Won't some kitchens end up with two ordering apps?

Only if you set it up that way, and mostly you should not. Leave the accounts that like Choco's app where they are and offer ours to the ones still on the phone. Calls keep coming to your desk as they do today, just without an order number from us, because only what is sent through our app gets one.
How soon can our accounts start?

Most distributors are up and running within 24 to 48 hours, and most of their customers place a first order that same day. There is no IT project, and Choco carries on as normal throughout, so there is no switch-over date to plan around.
What does adding VoiceOrder Solutions cost?

We quote each distributor separately and list no prices. Choco's own pricing page says it charges a monthly fee based on usage and asks you to talk to sales. Since you would be keeping Choco, the useful question is what the voice step adds on top, and a quote answers it.
Where do the Choco details on this page come from?

Choco's own site, read on 10 October 2026: the module names and descriptions off the homepage and the usage-based line off their pricing page. We have not repeated the growth figures they publish, because those are their numbers and not ours to vouch for. If any of it has moved on since, this page is what needs correcting.

hero.lead: Add voice ordering without giving anything up. VoiceOrder Solutions runs alongside Choco: kitchens talk through what they are short of in our app, confirm each item, then send. It lands on your desk numbered and dated, by email or straight into your system, while Choco keeps its storefront and customer tools.
